ideas.name: OhmWise
ideas.niche: Vintage audio component impedance matching and vacuum tube compatibility
ideas.problem: The high risk of damaging expensive vintage vacuum tube equipment due to incorrect impedance matching between amplifiers and speakers, or accidental misuse of non-equivalent vacuum tube replacements.
ideas.targetUser: Audiophile collectors, vintage audio restorers, and DIY enthusiasts (typically aged 35-65) who own mid-century tube gear and lack immediate access to technical datasheets.
coreFeatures: Impedance Match Safety Calculator
Tube Equivalence & Substitution Engine
Curated Vintage Gear Library
Visual Tube ID (OCR Scanner)
realDependencies: Curated Tube Datasheet API (e.g., a proprietary or scraped database of vacuum tube specs)
Computer Vision API (Google ML Kit or AWS Rekognition) for OCR tube identification
ideas.emulationStrategy: The demo will utilize a local 'MockDB' JSON file containing detailed technical specifications for 50 common tubes (e.g., 12AX7, EL34, 6L6) and 20 iconic vintage amplifiers. All data fetching will be wrapped in an async function that introduces a randomized 800ms to 1500ms delay to simulate real-world API latency. The OCR feature will be emulated through a 'Simulated Scan' text input; if the user types a tube model, the app will treat it as a successful camera scan and return the corresponding data from the MockDB. The Impedance Calculator will perform actual mathematical logic to ensure the results feel dynamic and authentic rather than hardcoded.

ideas.name: HideRescue
ideas.niche: Instant-response stain remediation for premium leather and suede goods.
ideas.problem: The decision paralysis and high risk of permanent damage caused by users searching for cleaning methods via long-form articles during an accidental spill.
ideas.targetUser: Luxury item owners (designer footwear, handbags, upholstery) and professionals in high-end hospitality who need immediate, expert-level guidance to prevent permanent material staining.
coreFeatures: Interactive Material Diagnostic Tree
One-Tap Substance Selection
Step-by-Step Emergency Protocols
Immediate 'Do Not Use' Warning Flags
Minimalist Emergency UI (High-contrast, large tap targets)
realDependencies: Computer Vision API for material/stain detection via camera
Affiliate Product API for specialized cleaning kits
Headless CMS for real-time protocol updates
ideas.emulationStrategy: The demo will utilize a local JSON lookup table to simulate the diagnostic logic. Image recognition will be emulated by triggering a 2.5-second 'Scanning Texture...' animation, after which the app will return a pre-determined 'High Confidence' match from a mock dataset. Network latency for product recommendations will be simulated using a 1-second artificial delay before populating the screen with hardcoded product strings and placeholder images.

ideas.name: LuxLogic
ideas.problem: The mathematical difficulty of translating desired visual moods into precise key-to-fill light intensity ratios on set, causing lighting inconsistency for solo operators.
ideas.targetUser: Indie solo filmmakers, film students, and aspiring cinematographers (ages 18-35) working in low-budget environments without a Gaffer or lighting crew.
coreFeatures: Mood-to-Ratio Presets (Instant math for High-key, Low-key, Noir, and Naturalistic styles)
F-Stop & EV Converter (Translates lighting ratios into actionable camera exposure adjustments)
Dynamic Shadow Intensity Visualizer (A real-time UI slider showing the visual depth of shadows based on the ratio)
Lighting Setup Log (A quick-save feature to store and recall specific ratio configurations for different scenes)
realDependencies: Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE) API for integration with digital light meters
Cloud Database (e.g., Firebase or Supabase) for multi-device setup synchronization
Computer Vision API for analyzing ambient light levels via the smartphone camera
ideas.emulationStrategy: The Bluetooth dependency will be emulated using a 'Mock Meter' toggle that streams randomized lux values through a simulated 800ms latency delay. Cloud synchronization will be faked using LocalStorage combined with a `setTimeout` wrapper to simulate network requests. The Computer Vision feature will be mocked by calculating the average pixel luminance of the device's camera preview feed rather than performing a deep-learning-based lighting analysis.

ideas.name: MimicMatch
ideas.niche: Visual-first morphological comparison for foraging safety
ideas.problem: Foraging wikis and guides are often text-heavy and cognitively demanding, making it difficult to perform rapid, high-stakes visual differentiation between edible species and toxic lookalikes while in the field.
ideas.targetUser: Amateur foragers and weekend hikers (ages 25-55) who are actively gathering wild food and need unambiguous, high-contrast visual confirmation to prevent accidental poisoning.
coreFeatures: Side-by-Side Morphological Split-View with highlighted anatomical callouts (e.g., gill attachment, cap texture)
High-Contrast 'Danger Mode' UI using aggressive color coding to distinguish toxic vs. edible traits
Offline-First Regional Species Library for use in remote areas without cellular service
Lookalike-Pair Search logic that allows users to search for an edible species to immediately see its 'danger twins'
realDependencies: Computer Vision API (e.g., iNaturalist or custom TensorFlow model) for image recognition
Geolocation API for localized species suggestions based on user coordinates
High-resolution Image CDN (e.g., Cloudinary) for fast asset delivery
Local SQLite/Realm database for robust offline storage
ideas.emulationStrategy: The demo will use a local JSON manifest containing pre-defined 'Lookalike Pair' objects. Each object will include hardcoded image URLs, XY coordinates for 'morphology hotspots' to simulate AI detection, and toxicity metadata. A mock 'Analysis Engine' will be implemented using a 2-second `setTimeout` to simulate computer vision processing, complete with a 'Scanning Morphological Markers...' loading state. Geolocation will be emulated via a 'Mock Region' selector that filters the local dataset between 'Pacific Northwest', 'Appalachia', and 'Boreal Forest'.

ideas.name: PhonoGrid
ideas.niche: Mobile-optimized IPA symbol input and transcription interface
ideas.problem: The lack of native, efficient IPA character support on mobile operating systems makes precise phonetic transcription extremely difficult for researchers and students in the field.
ideas.targetUser: Linguistics researchers, graduate students, speech-language pathologists, and phonology enthusiasts who need to transcribe speech on mobile devices during fieldwork or study.
coreFeatures: Categorized Symbol Grid: Tabbed interface for vowels, consonants, diacritics, and suprasegmentals.
Fuzzy-Search Autocomplete: Quick-access search bar that finds symbols by name (e.g., typing 'glottal' to find 'ʔ').
Macro Templates: One-tap insertion for complex, multi-character phonetic sequences.
Real-time Formatting Canvas: An active text area that manages proper Unicode stacking for diacritics.
Export/Clipboard Suite: Instant formatting and copying of transcriptions for use in LaTeX or Word documents.
realDependencies: Unicode Standard Database (for comprehensive phonetic mapping)
High-fidelity Text-to-Speech (TTS) API for phonetic playback
Local SQLite Database for offline transcription storage
ideas.emulationStrategy: The demo will use a local JSON manifest to act as the Unicode database. Search functionality will be simulated using a local filter function on this manifest with a 300ms 'loading' delay to mimic API latency. Cloud sync will be emulated by returning 'Success' or 'Network Error' objects via a mock async function. Audio playback will be handled by playing pre-recorded local audio clips mapped to specific character IDs to simulate the TTS API.
